message.content:
**Hydrogen (H₂)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has several key physical and chemical properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic Number** | 1 |
| **Molecular Formula** | H₂ (diatomic) |
| **Standard State at STP** | Gas |
| **Density** | ~0.0899 g/L (at 25 °C, 101.325 kPa) – lighter than air |
| **Melting Point** | −259.16 °C (−434.49 °F) |
| **Boiling Point** | −252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| **Specific Heat Capacity (gas)** | ≈14.304 J/(mol·K) at constant pressure |
| **Heat of Vaporization** | 8.29 kJ/mol |
| **Reactivity** | Extremely reactive; forms hydrides with metals; reacts violently with oxygen → water or oxides depending on conditions |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **Ionization Energy** | First ionization energy: 1312 kJ/mol |
| **Bond Dissociation Energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ/mol |
| **Spectral Lines** | Lyman series visible in UV; Balmer lines in visible spectrum (e.g., Hα line at 656 nm). |
| **Isotopes** | Commonly ^1H (protium), deuterium (^2H/D), tritium (^3H/T). Deuterium and tritium have nuclear spin differences affecting magnetic resonance spectra. |
| **Magnetic Properties** | Diamagnetic when diatomic; paramagnetism appears only under high‑field NMR due to unpaired electrons in excited states. |
| **Solubility in Water** | Very low (~0.00018 g/100 mL at room temperature); increases slightly with decreasing temperature. |

### Chemical Behavior Highlights

* **Combustion:**  
  \(2\,\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\,\text{H}_2\text{O}\) (Exothermic)

* **Formation of Hydride Compounds:**  
  With alkali/alkaline earth metals → ionic metal hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂).

* **Catalytic Role:**  
  Used as a reducing agent in many industrial processes (hydrodesulfurisation, ammonia synthesis via Haber process).

* **Energy Carrier Potential:**  
  When combined with catalysts, it can produce clean electricity through fuel cells:
  \(\text{Anode}: \,\text{H}_2 \rightarrow 2\,\text{H}^+ + 2\,e^-\\[4pt]
   \text{Cathode}: \,2\,\text{H}^+ + 2\,e^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\)
  Net reaction yields electrical work without CO₂ emissions.

---

These characteristics make hydrogen unique among elements—its lightness, reactivity, and potential as a clean-energy carrier keep scientists researching its applications across chemistry, physics, materials science, and engineering.
